Given a real valued function ' $f$ ' such that
$f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}\frac{\tan ^2\{x\}}{x^2-[x]^2} & \text{ for } x>0 \\ 1 & \text{ for } x=0 \\ \sqrt{\{x\} \cot \{x\}} & \text{ for } x < 0\end{array}\right.$
then
questions.solution: $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \sqrt{\{-h\} \cot \{-h\}}=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \sqrt{(1-h) \cot (1-h)}=\sqrt{\cot 1}\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} f(x)=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\tan ^2\{h\}}{h^2-[h]^2}=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\tan ^2 h}{h^2}=1\therefore \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} f(x)$ does not exist.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{l}x^2-1,0 < x < 2 \\ 2 x+3,2 \leq x < 3\end{array}\right.$, then the quadratic equation whose roots are $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{-}} f(x)$ and $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{+}} f(x)$ is
questions.solution:
Since, $f(x)= \begin{cases}x^2-1, & 0 < x < 2 \\ 2 x+3, & 2 \leq x < 3\end{cases}$
Now, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{-}} \left(x²-1\right)$
$\begin{aligned}\\ =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}\left[(2-h)^2-1\right]=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}\left[4+h²-4 h-1\right]\\ \\ =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}\left[h^2-4 h+3\right]=0-0+3=3 \\ \end{aligned}$
and $\lim _{x \rightarrow 222^{+}}f(x)=\lim _{x$→ 2^{+}}(2 x+3)$
$=$\lim _{h \rightarrow 0000}[2(2+h)+3]=\lim _{h → 0}[4+2 h+3]=7$
Hence the quadratic equation whose roots are 3 and 7 is given by $x^2-(3+7) x+(3+7)=0 \Rightarrow x²-10 x+21=0$

questions.q: The value of $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{1-\cos (1-\cos x)}{x^4}$ is
questions.solution: $1-\cos (1-\cos x)=2 \sin ^2\left(\frac{1-\cos x}{2}\right)=2 \sin ^2\left(\sin ^2 \frac{x}{2}\right)\therefore \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{1-\cos (1-\cos x)}{x^4}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{2 \sin ^2\left(\sin ^2 \frac{x}{2}\right)}{x^4}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{2 \sin ^2\left(\sin ^2 \frac{x}{2}\right)}{\left(\sin ^2 \frac{x}{2}\right)^2} \times \frac{\sin ^4 \frac{x}{2}}{\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^4 \times 16}=\frac{1}{8}$

questions.q: The value of $\lim_{x \to \dfrac{3\pi}{4}}\dfrac{4\sin^{2}xcosx - cosx + sinx}{sinx + cosx}$ is
questions.solution:
$L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{3\pi}{4}}\dfrac{4\sin^{2}xcosx - cosx + sinx}{sinx + cosx}$

$L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{3\pi}{4}}\dfrac{2sinx\left(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x + 2sinxcosx - 1\right) - cosx + sinx}{sinx + cosx}$

$L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{3\pi}{4}}\dfrac{2sinx\left[( sinx + cosx{)}^{2} - 1\right] - cosx + sinx}{sinx + cosx}$

$L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{3\pi}{4}}\dfrac{2sinx ( sinx + cosx{)}^{2} - 2sinx - cosx + sinx}{sinx + cosx}$

$L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{3\pi}{4}}\dfrac{\left(sinx + cosx\right)\left\{2sinx\left(sinx + cosx\right) - 1\right\}}{sinx + cosx}$

$L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{3\pi}{4}}2sinx\left(sinx + cosx\right) - 1 = - 1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $a$, so that $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1}{x2}\left(e^{ax} - e^{x} - x\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}$,& is
questions.solution:
We have,

$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1}{x2}\left(e^{ax} - e^{x} - x\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{ae^{ax} - e^{x} - 1}{2x}\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}$ (using $L$'Hospital rule to the left hand side)

As $x \to 0$, the denominator is zero& and as the value of the limit is finite so, numerator must be zero for $x \to 0$.

Hence, $a - 1 - 1 = 0 ⇒ a = 2$.

questions.q: $\lim_{n \to \infty}sin \left[\pi\sqrt{n^{2} + 1}\right] is equal to$
questions.solution:
$\lim_{n \to \infty}sin\left\{n\pi\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{n2}\right)^{1} / 2\right\}$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}sin\left\{n\pi\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{2n^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{8n^{4}} + \ldots\right)\right\}$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}sin\left\{n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{2n} - \dfrac{\pi}{8n^{3}} + \ldots\right\}$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\left(- 1\right)nsin\pi\left(\dfrac{1}{2n} - \dfrac{1}{8n^{3}} + \ldots\right) = 0$

questions.q: If $\lim_{n \to \infty}\left(an - \dfrac{1 + n^{2}}{1 + n}\right) = b$, where $a$ is finite number, then
questions.solution:
$\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{an ( 1 + n ) - \left(1 + n^{2}\right)}{1 + n}$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{( a - 1 ) n^{2} + an - 1}{n + 1} = \infty$,

If $a - 1 \ne 0$ limit does not exist and if $a - 1 = 0$, then

$\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{an - 1}{n + 1} = a = b$

$⇒ a = b = 1$

questions.q: $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\int_{0}^{2 x} x e^{x^{2}} d x}{e^{4 x^{2}}} $$\text{ equals }$
questions.solution: Consider $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\int_{0}^{2 x} x e^{x^{2}} d x}{e^{4 x^{2}}} \begin{array}{l} =\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{2 \int_{0}^{2 x} x e^{x^{2}} d x}{2 e^{4 x^{2}}}$\\ =$\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{2 \int_{0}^{2 x} e^{x^{2}} d\left(x^{2}\right)}{2 e^{4 x^{2}}}$\\ =$\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\left[e^{x^{2}}\right]_{0}^{2 x}}{e^{4 x^{2}}}=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{e^{4 x^{2}}-1}{2 e^{4 x^{2}}}$\\ =$\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2 e^{4 x^{2}}}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \end{array}$

questions.q: If $\lim _{x \rightarrow} x \sin \left(\frac{1}{x}\right)=A$ and $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} x \sin \left(\frac{1}{x}\right)=B$, then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution: As given, $\mathrm{A}=\lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \infty} \mathrm{x} \sin \left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)=\lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\sin \left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)}{\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)}$ Let $\mathrm{t}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}$ when $\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \alpha, \mathrm{t} \rightarrow 0 \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow\mathrm{A}$&=$\lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\sin \mathrm{t}}{\mathrm{t}}=1 \\ \text{$ and $} \left[\because \lim _{\mathrm{t} \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin \mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{x}}=1\right] \end{aligned} and \mathrm{B}=\lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow 0} \mathrm{x} \sin \left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right) \Rightarrow \mathrm{B}=\lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow 0} \mathrm{x} \cdot \lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow 0} \sin \left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right) \Rightarrow \mathrm{B}=0$\therefore \quad A=1 and B=0$ is correct$

questions.q: $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}(\operatorname{cosec} x)^{1 / \log x}$ is equal to :
questions.solution: Let $y=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}(\operatorname{cosec} x)^{1 / \log x}$ Taking $\log$ on both sides, we get $\log y=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\log \operatorname{cosec} x}{\log x}\left[\frac{\infty}{\infty}\right.$ form $]=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{-\cot x}{1 / x} \quad$ (ByL' Hospital rule) $=-\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{x}{\tan x} \quad\left(\because \cot x=\frac{1}{\tan x}\right)\Rightarrow \log y=-1\Rightarrow y=e^{-1}=\frac{1}{e}$ Hence, required limit $=\frac{1}{e}$

questions.solution: Given $f(x)=g(x) h(x)\Rightarrow h(x)=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}\Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 1} h(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{f(x)}{g(x)}\Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{\left(x^{5}-1\right)\left(x^{3}+1\right)}{\left(x^{2}-1\right)\left(x^{2}-x+1\right)}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{x^{5}-1^{5}}{x-1}=5 \times 1^{4}=5$
